slides.title: Fast comes from tricks
slides.text: Fast facts are not magic memory. Every fast counter uses tricks: doubling, halving, and building a hard fact from an easy one.

focus.cue: Start from a fact you know: 7 x 2 = 14.

slides.title: Rough first, then build
slides.text: Rough first: 9 x 7 is a bit under 70. Build it from the easy fact 9 x 5.

visual.label: Building 9 x 7 from 9 x 5: 45 plus 18 makes 63

focus.cue: Start with a fact you know: 9 x 5 = 45.

slides.title: Facts travel in families
slides.text: Multiplication and division are one family. If 5 x 9 = 45, then 45 shared by 9 is 5, and 45 shared by 5 is 9.

visual.label: One fact family: 5 x 9 = 45, 45 shared by 9 is 5, 45 shared by 5 is 9

focus.cue: Turn it around: 45 shared by 5 is 9.

slides.title: The Jumble races itself
slides.text: The Jumble tried to race by memorizing every fact alone. It mixed up 7 x 8 for a week, until it learned the trick: double 7 x 4.

slides.title: Stretch: Doubling chains
slides.text: Doubling is a ladder. 6 x 8 is double 6 x 4, and 6 x 4 is double 6 x 2. Climb down to a fact you know, then climb back up.

visual.label: Doubling chains: 6 x 2, then double to 6 x 4, then double to 6 x 8

focus.cue: Climb down to a fact you know: 6 x 2 = 12.
Climb back up: double 24 and 6 x 8 = 48.

words.means: able to answer smoothly, with a strategy that works
to make a number twice as big, or the result
a plan or trick you choose on purpose
multiplication and division facts built from the same numbers

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Sum Racer. It opens on the Mixed Grand Prix track, a mix of everything, and it stays there. Win the race against your own best, and name the trick behind each hard fact.
